title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, numbered 176 and headed 'IX', section 13.4. It is not part of the handwritten de Rham/divided-power notes around it (the previous page is a handwritten computation about Hom^{-d}(τ_α M, N) factoring through the divisible part). It is most likely a typescript sheet reused as scrap paper. Handwriting shows through from the verso, and the sheet carries the archive number 494. The content fits a transcendental section of SGA 7 Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), though I am not certain of this.

Setting:
- S is a complex analytic space and A is a commutative analytic group over S.
- E̲ = Lie(A) is the Lie-algebra sheaf (a vector bundle).
- R̲ is the kernel of the exponential exp: E̲ → A, a sheaf of finitely generated free ℤ-modules (the 'H_1' of the fibres).
- There is a canonical map 𝓔 = R̲ ⊗_ℤ O_S → E̲. Its kernel is F̲(A), giving 0 → F̲ → 𝓔 → E̲.

Main case: the map is surjective, i.e. each R_s spans E_s over ℂ.
- Then 0 → F̲ → 𝓔 → E̲ → 0 is exact.
- If R is locally constant, this is a short exact sequence of locally free O_S-modules.
- The data (E, R) are then equivalent to the data (R, F̲): a local system of lattices R together with a locally direct-summand subbundle F̲ ⊂ R ⊗ O_S such that F̲ ∩ R̲ = 0.
- 𝓔 carries a three-step 'Hodge filtration': Fil^1 = 𝓔, Fil^0 = F̲, Fil^{-1} = 0.
- The construction is functorial in A and compatible with arbitrary base change.

In modern terms, this is the standard dictionary between families of (possibly non-compact) complex commutative Lie groups of the form E/R and variations of mixed Hodge-type data on H_1. When R has full rank it is a polarizable-or-not VHS of weight -1, with F̲ = F^0 H_1 and Lie A = H_1/F^0. This is the transcendental counterpart of Deligne's 1-motives and of Grothendieck's own crystalline Dieudonné theory, where Lie A = H_1/Fil. It serves the comparison of Néron models and monodromy over a complex base with their Hodge-theoretic description.
errors: The condition F̲ ∩ R̲ = 0 (13.4.5) only guarantees that R_s → E_s is injective, not that its image is discrete. Example: R = ℤ², E = ℂ, with the generators mapping to (1, √2). To recover an analytic (Hausdorff) group E/R from (R, F̲), one needs F_s ∩ (R_s ⊗ ℝ) = 0 fibrewise, i.e. R_s ⊗ ℝ → E_s injective. In the direction (E, R) → (R, F̲) this holds automatically because R is the kernel of exp. So the claimed equivalence is incomplete as stated, unless 13.4.5 is meant in the stronger real sense.
The filtration indexing Fil^1 ⊃ Fil^0 ⊃ Fil^{-1} is increasing and shifted relative to the modern convention for H_1, where F^{-1} = H_1, F^0 = H^{0,-1}-part, F^1 = 0. This is notational only.

ideas.what: Description of a family of analytic groups A = E/R over S via the lattice R and the kernel F of R⊗O_S → Lie A, with a Hodge filtration
ideas.modern_name: Variation of Hodge structure of type {(-1,0),(0,-1)} attached to a family of complex tori / complex Lie groups; transcendental 1-motive data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann, Lefschetz) for single tori; Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II/III, 1971-74) for families and 1-motives
ideas.where_published: Likely SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (LNM 288, 1972), transcendental section; unsure of exact numbering

ideas.what: Functoriality and base-change compatibility of the sequence 0→F→R⊗O_S→Lie A
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration on H_1 of a family of complex tori, functorial in the group

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page from what appears to be a published or circulated text (probably SGA 7 Exp. IX), reused as scrap paper in the de Rham notes. Its content is the standard lattice/Hodge-filtration description of families of complex tori. Its only slight interest is that it parallels the crystalline Dieudonné picture (Lie = H_1/Fil) behind the 1976 divided-power talk.
transcription_corrections: The typed '𝓔 = R̲⊗_ℤ O̲_S' in (13.4.2) has an overstrike on R/⊗ in the original. The transcription is correct in meaning.
Archive stamp '494' and handwritten '45' at the bottom are archival page markers, not mathematics. The faint handwriting visible in the background is bleed-through from the verso (manuscript side).
